transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you. ...Well, my job sent me. I guess I've been missing things lately. Work orders, mostly. And scheduled callbacks. 

I just keep forgetting the basic follow-ups I promise people, and... it kind of piled up on me. They told me I had to come here to get it sorted out, or I'm gonna lose my shot at moving up.
Have you had this kind of trouble with attention or forgetting things since you were a kid?

Yeah, I guess so. Um... I remember being like this back in grade school. Long before any of this work stuff. Teachers always told my parents I was bright, but... I don't know, I was always losing my papers. Or I'd miss parts of the instructions and they'd have to remind me to finish my work. So... yeah, it's been a while.
How often do you use alcohol or marijuana?
Um... I don't. I mean, I don't use marijuana at all. And alcohol... not really. Just... no.
Outside of work, do you also have trouble staying organized in day-to-day life?
Um... I don't really know. I guess things at home are... fine. I mean, I get by okay. It's not really something I think about much.
Do these problems with forgetting and missing things also cause trouble in your personal life, not just at work?

Um... not really my personal life. It's... mostly just work. It's gotten pretty bad there, honestly. I've got a big backlog of work orders, and... some tenants have been complaining. I even got a safety review on my record recently because of it. It's... I don't know, I'm just worried it's going to mess up my chances for a promotion. I've been trying really hard for it.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge at work?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I wouldn't say I feel anxious. Just... stressed about the backlog, I guess. But no.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Um... no. Not depressed. I don't... I don't really get like that. Just stressed about my job, like I said.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern since grade school of inattentive symptoms including losing papers, missing parts of instructions, needing reminders to finish work, and current occupational problems with forgetting work orders and scheduled callbacks. Substance use, anxiety, and depressive symptoms were denied as primary explanations. Although cross-situational impairment outside work was not clearly endorsed, the interview supports ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation as the best-fitting diagnosis among the candidates provided.
